data.label: Hiring Guide
data.title:
5 questions to ask before
you *hire a designer*
data.sub: Don't waste your budget. Swipe to learn →

data.label: Sign #1
data.title: Who *owns the site*?
data.body: If you don't own the domain and hosting, you're trapped. You should always have full administrative control over your digital property.
data.fix: Fix: Ensure your name is on the domain registration.

data.label: Sign #2
data.title: Can I *make simple edits*?
data.body: You shouldn't have to call a developer just to change a phone number. You need a site that is easy to update.
data.fix: Fix: Ask for a walkthrough of the editing dashboard.

data.label: Sign #3
data.title: Is it *mobile friendly*?
data.body: Most customers will find your business on their phones first. If the site is hard to use, they will leave immediately.
data.fix: Fix: Test their portfolio sites on your own phone.

data.label: Sign #4
data.title: How is *SEO handled*?
data.body: A pretty site is useless if customers can't find you on Google. Your designer must build with search visibility in mind.
data.fix: Fix: Ask how they handle basic local keywords.

data.label: Sign #5
data.title: What is the *ongoing support*?
data.body: Websites need maintenance to stay secure and fast. Clarify if they offer long-term help or disappear after launch.
data.fix: Fix: Get their maintenance pricing in writing upfront.
